Let $ inom{2k}{k}$ denote the central binomial coefficient and $\left( rac{\cdot}{p}ight)$ the Legendre symbol. Prove or disprove the following two-part conjecture.

(i) For every prime $p 
otin \{2,5\}$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}  rac{21k^3 + 22k^2 + 8k + 1}{256^{k}}  inom{2k}{k}^{7} \equiv p^3 \pmod{p^8},$$
and
$$\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}  rac{168k^3 + 76k^2 + 14k + 1}{2^{20k}}  inom{2k}{k}^{7} \equiv \left( rac{-1}{p}ight) p^3 \pmod{p^8}.$$

(ii) For every integer $n > 1$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (21k^3 + 22k^2 + 8k + 1)\, inom{2k}{k}^{7} \, 256^{\,n-1-k} \equiv 0 \pmod{2 n^3  inom{2n}{n}^{3}},$$
and
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (168k^3 + 76k^2 + 14k + 1)\, inom{2k}{k}^{7} \, 2^{20(n-1-k)} \equiv 0 \pmod{2 n^3  inom{2n}{n}^{3}}.$$

Related supercongruence conjectures by Z.-W. Sun have been partially resolved in various papers, but no source specifically establishing this pair of mod $p^8$ supercongruences and the divisibility statement was located. The status appears to remain unresolved, but this could not be confirmed definitively.
